source_title: Policy on Compassionate Leave for Postgraduate Research Degree students
question: One of our PGR students has been bereaved. What leave can they take, and what happens if they need longer than that?
expected_answer: Compassionate leave can be sought for up to two weeks (10 working days), and the standard and maximum periods of study and the thesis submission date are automatically extended by the duration of the approved compassionate leave. If the longer-term impact requires a longer period of leave, the Policy on Leave of Absence (intermission) should be consulted instead - that is a separate policy with its own grounds and procedures.
follow_up_question: They may need longer than that, and they're part-time - does the part-time mode reduce what they can take?
follow_up_expected_answer: No. For longer leave the Policy on Leave of Absence (intermission) applies, and periods of intermission are not impacted or determined by a student's mode of study - the maximum allowance in terms remains the same for full- and part-time students.

source_title: Policy on Leave of Absence (intermission) for Postgraduate Research Degree students
question: A PGR student sponsored on a Student visa wants to intermit for two terms. What are the consequences?
expected_answer: The University is required to withdraw sponsorship from a student who intermits, and the Home Office will curtail their immigration permission. The student will have to leave the UK while intermitting, and must stop any work immediately because the condition allowing work alongside study no longer applies. Before returning they can request further immigration sponsorship and, if eligible, apply for a new Student visa. Retrospective intermission is not possible for sponsored students.
follow_up_question: While they are registered, are there rules about how their supervision meetings must be held because they are visa-sponsored?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. For students with immigration sponsorship the majority of contact should be face-to-face; in exceptional circumstances the University may agree contact via video link, and virtual meetings must not breach progress monitoring requirements for students subject to immigration control.
follow_up_keyphrases: majority of contact should be face-to-face

source_title: Policy on Thesis Submission, Deposit and Retention
question: Our student intends to submit their thesis at the end of their completion period. What do they need to do in advance, and how much notice is required?
expected_answer: They must give the Postgraduate Research Education Team at least three months' notice of their intention to submit, via the Approval of Title form, which the PGRE Team needs to begin appointing examiners. Submitting it late is likely to delay the examination process. A student entering a completion period does so on the understanding that the full thesis will be ready for submission by the end of that period.
follow_up_question: They still owe some fees - does that matter?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. All registration fees and debts must be paid before the thesis can be accepted for submission.
follow_up_keyphrases: before the thesis can be accepted

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: If the RSPB recommends a one-term extension to a student's standard period, how does that affect their completion time and their submission deadline?
expected_answer: The RSPB can recommend an extension of up to one term where milestone requirements for entering a completion period have not been met. The subsequent number of completion periods available is reduced by one term, unless exceptional circumstances make that reduction inappropriate, and the student must be offered the chance to discuss this with the RSPB before the recommendation goes to the Dean. For candidates first registered from October 2018 onwards the submission deadline is the end of the standard period of study, so extending that period moves the deadline.
keyphrases: end of the standard period of study
follow_up_question: Is the deadline the same for someone who registered before 2018?
follow_up_expected_answer: No. For candidates first registered before October 2018 the submission deadline of the thesis for examination is the end of the completion period, rather than the end of the standard period of study.

source_title: Policy on Leave of Absence (intermission) for Postgraduate Research Degree students
question: A first-year PGR student is asking for three terms of leave. Is that possible, and is there a shorter option?
expected_answer: It is possible but consequential: if a student requests a leave of absence during their first year of study which extends for longer than two terms, they will be required to restart the course. For short-term needs following bereavement or the serious illness of a close relative, compassionate leave of up to two weeks is a separate and lighter-touch option that automatically extends the study periods and submission date.
follow_up_question: If the reason is illness, how is that decided?
follow_up_expected_answer: Requests for intermission due to ill health are judged on a case-by-case basis. If the case is sound and backed by medical evidence, leave of absence is generally agreed regardless of the stage of the degree, with the length depending on the illness and its severity.

source_title: Policy for the Appointment of Independent Chairs for Research Degree Vivas
question: A thesis was referred and the student has now resubmitted. Do we need an Independent Chair for the second viva, and can the viva be waived?
expected_answer: Two separate rules apply. An Independent Chair is appointed where the viva follows a referral and resubmission of a thesis, so yes. On waiving, where the recommendation on the referred thesis is a pass, a request by the examiners to waive the viva will normally be granted; where the recommendation is not a pass, a waiver will only be granted in exceptional circumstances.
follow_up_question: Who can be the Independent Chair - can it be someone from the same department?
follow_up_expected_answer: No. The Independent Chair will be from outside the candidate's department and will have no conflict of interest with the candidate, the supervisor or the External Examiner. A nominee must be a permanent member of staff who has been an Internal Examiner for at least two postgraduate research examinations at Essex, or has examined two theses externally and undertaken University of Essex Independent Chair training.
follow_up_keyphrases: at least two postgraduate research examinations

source_title: Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates for the Tavistock and Portman NHS Foundation Trust 2025-26
question: A Tavistock professional doctorate student needs an extension to their standard period. Who recommends it and which Dean approves it?
expected_answer: The recommendation can only be made by the RSPB - a decision or recommendation to extend the standard period, like discontinuation, downgrading or permitting entry into completion, can only be made by the RSPB. For Tavistock and Portman programmes 'Dean' means the Dean of Partnerships (or their deputy), so approval is sought there rather than from the Executive Dean.
keyphrases: can only be made by the RSPB
follow_up_question: Is that a different route from an Essex-based professional doctorate?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes in respect of the Dean and the reporting line. On Essex professional doctorates the Professional Doctorate Director is responsible to the Head of Department and most decisions are referred to the Faculty Dean Postgraduate; for the Trust programmes the Course Lead is responsible to the Portfolio Manager and decisions go to the Dean of Partnerships. The RSPB-only rule for these decisions is the same in both.

source_title: Code of Practice: Postgraduate Research Degrees
question: We want a visiting academic to supervise a research student. Could they instead act as Independent Chair at a viva?
expected_answer: Visiting staff cannot be appointed as a supervisor of a PGR student unless formally appointed via the associate supervisor route. Nor could they be an Independent Chair: a nominee must be a permanent member of staff who has been an Internal Examiner for at least two postgraduate research examinations at Essex, or has examined two theses externally and undertaken University of Essex Independent Chair training.
follow_up_question: If the supervisor is inexperienced, does that change who should chair the Supervisory Panel?
follow_up_expected_answer: Yes. Where the supervisor is a less experienced member of staff who has not supervised a student through to completion, the chair must be an experienced supervisor.
follow_up_keyphrases: chair must be an experienced supervisor

question: Our internal examiner has never examined a research degree before. What does that mean for how the viva is run?
expected_answer: An Independent Chair will be appointed: the Faculty Dean (Postgraduate) appoints one where the Internal Examiner has no experience in research degree examining, or is new to research degree examining at Essex and has not undertaken Internal Examiner training. The Independent Chair oversees the conduct of the oral examination. If the viva runs longer than two hours the internal examiner or Independent Chair will recommend an adjournment for a break.
keyphrases: no experience in research degree examining
follow_up_question: Can the supervisor sit in to support the inexperienced examiner?
follow_up_expected_answer: Not normally. The candidate's supervisor will not normally be present at the viva and can only be present in exceptional circumstances, approved on an individual basis by the Faculty Dean (Postgraduate) and with the agreement of the examiners. It is good practice for the supervisor to be invited in at the end when the examiners communicate their recommendation.

source_title: Policy on Thesis Submission, Deposit and Retention
question: How should a professional doctorate candidate submit their thesis, and what happens next in the examination process?
expected_answer: All candidates for Masters by Dissertation, MPhil, MD, PhD and Professional Doctorate must submit the thesis electronically in PDF format, contained within one document rather than separate files, emailed to the Postgraduate Research Team at pgrsubmission@essex.ac.uk, with all registration fees and debts paid first. The examination then proceeds to the viva, whose format is agreed between the participants starting from the candidate's preference.
follow_up_question: Who decides whether the viva is in person or online?
follow_up_expected_answer: The candidate may express a preference which the department should seek to accommodate. The person or team arranging the viva should liaise with all participants and seek agreement from all parties on the viva format, starting with the candidate's preference.
